Norwegian Media & Publishing Industry Hit by Norovirus Outbreak, Causing Widespread Disruptions

A sudden norovirus outbreak has swept through Norway’s Media & Publishing industry this week, forcing several newsrooms, printing plants, and publishing offices to close temporarily or operate with significantly reduced staff. The highly contagious virus, which causes acute gastroenteritis, has affected workers at multiple sites in Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim, and Stavanger.

According to the Norwegian Publishing Federation, at least 23 percent of industry employees in the Oslo metropolitan area reported symptoms as of Wednesday, prompting leading firms such as Nyhetsparti AS and Fjordpressen to implement emergency remote work protocols. “We have never seen so many staff call in sick in such a short time,” said Liv Røed, human resources manager at Fjordpressen. “Editorial deadlines are being pushed back, and we are struggling to maintain our regular publishing schedules.”

Printing operations have also been severely impacted. At Nordprinten’s central facility in Bergen, over half of the shift workers were absent on Tuesday. “We’re running at about 40 percent capacity,” said site manager Eirik Holme. “We’ve had to delay delivery of several weekly magazines and postpone special print runs.”

Industry analysts say the timing is particularly challenging, as many publishers are preparing for their summer issues. “The backlog is building up, and there is a risk of significant revenue loss if periodicals miss their time-sensitive windows,” said Sanna Lie, a media sector analyst at Innlandsforskning. “The industry is already stretched thin by ongoing digital transitions, so this outbreak adds to existing pressures.”

Trade unions have called for enhanced sanitation measures at all media sites and are urging firms to provide paid sick leave and flexible work options to affected employees. “Our primary concern is the health and safety of workers,” said Grete Sundby, spokesperson for the Media Workers’ Union. “We are monitoring the situation closely and expect employers to prioritize containment.”

Health authorities continue to investigate the outbreak’s source within the industry. As the situation evolves, many firms anticipate further delays in publication and distribution schedules in the days ahead.
